Element.attribute: Define the control structure for the program
Define the control structure for the program

Confirm the executive sponsor, program sponsor, program manager, and other key members
of the program management and control structure.

To facilitate program communications and decision-making, there should be one program
sponsor and one program manager for the program.

The program sponsor should be a manager in the appropriate area of the business. The
specific managerial level of this person should correspond with the importance and visibility
of the program.

The program manager should possess the relevant skills and experience to successfully
manage the program and, if possible, should be familiar with the enterprise's business or a
similar business.

Define any other review groups or individuals who will be involved in managing the
program.

If the enterprise has an existing management and control structure, map the methodology
roles to it.

Element.attribute: Identify the participating managers and liaison personnel
Identify the participating managers and liaison personnel

Identify personnel who should be consulted or kept abreast of the status and results of the
project.

Notify all personnel identified as key participants of their appointments. Provide them with a
summary of the roles they are expected to play and an estimate of the length of their
involvement.

Element.Name: Define reporting requirements

Privacy Notice

Powered by Global Methods in conjunction with Consulting Methods
Element.attribute:
• Define the reporting requirements for the project.
    • Reporting requirements include the following:
      • Type of information required for each recipient
      • Frequency of the reporting
      • Medium (e.g., written, oral)
      • Special considerations

Considerations include deviations from plans that fall outside the normal scope of periodic reports. These deviations may be too important or urgent to be tabled until the next periodic report is issued.

  • Review the reporting requirements with each of the recipients to confirm that their needs are met.
